issues.description: In the template dd.py, the ComputeTable.table attribute is annotated as a list type (list[tuple[DD, DD, DDOperation, DD]]) but the implementation initializes and uses it as a dictionary (self.table = {}; lookup/insert expect dict semantics). This annotation is inconsistent with the code and with the reference solution, where ComputeTable.table is correctly annotated as dict[tuple[DD, DD, DDOperation], DD]. The incorrect annotation in the template can confuse students reading type hints and may lead to static type-checker warnings.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the template annotation to match the intended dictionary usage. Change the ComputeTable.table annotation in template_repository/dd.py from list[tuple[DD, DD, DDOperation, DD]] to dict[tuple[DD, DD, DDOperation], DD] (as in the solution). This aligns type hints with the runtime behavior and the reference solution, avoiding confusion and static type-checker errors.
